research_contract.question: How do we increase the People Graph's research and decision value by 100× without treating row count as value or weakening identity quality, provenance, rights, privacy, reproducibility, and reversibility?
source_scopes: SISO People Graph code and contract at de048bb3b34bf931b56fd741cb46c1334acdfb98
SISO Book Library code and contract at be9ab0831b9ea8802d6898f3a3dfa8a61c63e80b
Publication-safe outputs from the thirteen named parallel lanes and their draft handoffs
Public or authorized source observations expressed through pg-observation-0.1; raw restricted payloads remain outside the registry
research_contract.decision_to_change: Choose which source classes, identity methods, temporal and claim layers, query surfaces, and operating loops to fund, merge, revise, or kill for the next evidence-backed People Graph release.
success_criteria: Breadth: demonstrate at least tenfold source-native observation coverage across four distinct source classes, with every promoted observation carrying source, native identifier, observed-at time, rights state, provenance, and receipt references.

Resolution quality: on a versioned stratified benchmark, auto-accepted identity links achieve at least 99.5% precision, recall and abstention are reported separately, and every accepted merge or alias remains reversible with literal evidence.

Research depth: for at least 100 prioritized people or 25 named research questions, expose a three-layer path from raw observation to cited claim to explicit adjudication, with no unsupported cross-source assertion presented as fact.

Decision value: in at least five pre-registered operator or research decisions, the graph changes the selected action or reduces evidence-retrieval time by at least 80% against a measured baseline; additional rows alone cannot satisfy this criterion.

Rights and privacy: every promoted observation has an explicit rights state, restricted or discovery-only material never appears as a public payload, and living-person data is limited to justified public or authorized evidence.
Reproducibility and cost: the accepted increment rebuilds from versioned manifests, produces comparable quality reports, and stays within a declared per-source acquisition and refresh budget.
falsifiers: Source expansion increases rows or edges by at least tenfold but produces no measured improvement in the five decision-use cases.
Auto-accepted identity precision falls below 99.5%, accepted links cannot be reversed, or ambiguous names are silently merged.
Any promoted public record lacks a rights state, leaks restricted payloads, or exposes unjustified sensitive information about a living person.
New source pilots mostly duplicate existing low-signal entities and cannot produce replayable source-native observations with receipts.
The graph remains a collection of names and topics without cited claims, temporal context, contradiction handling, or adjudication.
Refresh and build costs exceed the declared budget without a proportional improvement in resolution, research depth, or decision value.
evidence_gaps: There is no agreed baseline for current evidence-retrieval time, decision changes, or operator utility.
The exact People Graph source commit has not been proven as a clean reproducible build in this registry lane, and the reviewed v2 builder's schema path does not match the tracked schema location.
A versioned identity-resolution benchmark with precision, recall, abstention, collision, living-person, and historical-person strata is not yet published.
Source-specific terms, privacy, retention, and redistribution rules are incomplete for the proposed scholarly, software, AI, creator, and media pilots.
The pg-observation-0.1 interchange has not yet been exercised end to end through Foundry discovery, Evidence Engine adjudication, and canonical graph admission.
Historical references under a different GitHub owner remain a verification and migration question rather than an assumed alias.
watch_triggers: Any identity benchmark regression, disputed auto-merge, rollback, or evidence-loss incident.
Any source terms, rights, privacy, API, rate-limit, or retention change that alters admissible observations.
A parallel source pilot publishes a replayable observation set and draft handoff.
The v3 schema, identity, query, claims, build, or integration lane publishes a compatibility contract.
The first five decision-use cases receive measured baselines and post-change outcomes.
Review at least monthly until a first Answer Release, and immediately after a material source, schema, quality, or governance change.
research_contract.answer_shape: A source-by-source and capability-by-capability decision matrix separating breadth, resolution quality, research depth, decision value, rights and privacy, reproducibility, and cost, with explicit fund, merge, revise, or kill recommendations and traceable evidence.
research_contract.refresh_policy: Reassess on every material lane handoff and at least monthly until a first evidenced Answer Release; afterward refresh on source-contract, rights, schema, identity-quality, cost, or decision-utility triggers.

evidence.summary: The requested program separates breadth, resolution, research depth, and decision value; requires measurable kill criteria; and launches thirteen no-wait parallel lanes.
The authored lane manifest records branches, exclusive path zones, current-main starts, and draft-PR handoffs.
